Below is a quick reference for the **long‑weekend** holidays in Canada for the calendar year 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined here as a federal holiday that falls on a **Friday or Monday**, thereby extending the regular Saturday‑Sunday weekend into a three‑day break.  

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Day of Week | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------------|-------|
| **Feb 20** | Family Day (observed in AB, SK, MB, ON, NB, PEI) | Monday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| **Mar 31** | Good Friday (most provinces, except QC) | Friday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | Monday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| **Sep 04** | Labour Day | Monday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| **Oct 09** | Thanksgiving | Monday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas Day | Monday | Creates a 3‑day weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |

### Holidays that fall on weekend days (but are *not* long weekends by the strict definition)

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Day of Week | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------------|-------|
| **Jul 01** | Canada Day | Saturday | Holiday on a weekend day – often treated as a “holiday weekend” by many Canadians |
| **Nov 11** | Remembrance Day | Thursday | Holiday on a weekday – can be combined with Friday for a 4‑day break if you take the day off |

> **Quick recap:**  
> • **Long weekends (strict definition):** 6 holidays listed in the first table.  
> • **Other notable holidays:** Canada Day (Saturday) and Remembrance Day (Thursday) are federal holidays that may influence travel plans but don’t automatically create a 3‑day weekend.

Feel free to copy the tables into your holiday‑planning app or let me know if you’d like the data in a different format (CSV, JSON, etc.).
